# Adjudication Task — Chapter 950

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃950화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|모두에게 있어, 그해 여름은 유난히도 짧고 혼란스러웠다.
  6|
  7|이상할 정도로 변덕스러워진 날씨는 여러 이유 중 하나에 불과했다.
  8|
  9|이제 홍수는 그리 놀라운 축에도 들지 못한다.
 10|
 11|한여름의 어느 날에는 장맛비 대신 우박이 쏟아지기도 했고, 사상 최대의 폭염(暴炎)에 이어 새하얀 서리가 내려앉은 적도 있었으니까.
 12|
 13|하루아침에 농사를 망친 이들은 주저앉아 통곡했고, 폭등하는 곡물값에 당장 내일의 끼니를 걱정할 처지가 되었다.
 14|
 15|관부에서는 구휼미(救恤米)를 풀었으나 한 가마니의 쌀은 몇 사람의 손을 거쳐 한 홉으로 줄어들었다.
 16|
 17|결국 굶주림을 참지 못한 이들은 산으로 향했다.
 18|
 19|그곳에서 나무껍질을 벗겨 먹거나, 녹슨 농기구를 무기 삼아 산적이 되었다.
 20|
 21|그러나 그마저도 얼마 가지 못할 것이다.
 22|
 23|일평생 우직하게 논밭만 일구던 그들이 무엇을 할 수 있을까. 어설픈 산적을 기다리고 있는 것은 죽음뿐이다.
 24|
 25|관군이건 무림인이건, 그들은 언젠가 토벌될 것이고 차가운 날붙이가 몸뚱어리를 가르는 순간에 이르러서야 문득 한 가지 의문을 떠올릴 터였다.
 26|
 27|자신이 어째서 이렇게 된 걸까, 하는 의문을.
 28|
 29|하지만 누구도 그 의문에 대한 답을 알지 못한다.
 30|
 31|이 광활한 천하에서 벌어지는 일들은 종종 아무도 이해할 수 없을 정도로 난해하니까.
 32|
 33|특히 지난 이 년간의 일을 돌이켜 보면 더더욱 그러했다.
 34|
 35|“그 이야기 들었나? 불과 두어 달 전에 남만에서…….”
 36|
 37|“그뿐만이 아닐세. 광서 땅이 피로 물들었어.”
 38|
 39|“미치겠군. 세상이 어찌 돌아가는지.”
 40|
 41|어딜 가나 숱한 이야기가 떠도는 것은 흔한 일이다.
 42|
 43|그러나 몇 년 전과는 분위기가, 아니 공기부터가 달랐다.
 44|
 45|객잔 안을 가득 채운 사람들의 목소리는 새벽 안개처럼 낮게 가라앉아 있었고, 눈빛과 얼굴에는 숨길 수 없는 근심으로 가득했다.
 46|
 47|한때는 술안주요, 흥밋거리에 불과했던 무림의 소문들은 이제 현실의 칼날이 되어 조금씩 살갗을 파고들고 있었다.
 48|
 49|그들은 더는 웃고 노래하지 못했다.
 50|
 51|수십여 명씩 무리 지어 거리를 순찰하는 관군과 간혹 스쳐 지나가는 무림인들을 불안한 눈빛으로 바라보며, 날이 저물기 전에 집으로 향하는 발걸음을 재촉했다.
 52|
 53|이제는 모두가 본능적으로 알고 있었다.
 54|
 55|새로운 전란(戰亂)은 이미 시작되었다는 것을.
 56|
 57|수십여 년 전 중원을 짓밟았던 십만의 마교도(魔敎徒)와는 비교도 안 될 재앙이, 자신들의 머리 위로 드리워지고 있다는 사실을.
 58|
 59|그리고 무림이라는 울타리에 몸담은 이들은 작금의 현실을 누구보다 선명하고 또렷하게 느끼고 있었다.
 60|
 61|“놈들이 이제 황실에까지 손을 뻗쳤다는군. 그것도 정마대전 무렵부터 장장 수십여 년간이나.”
 62|
 63|“나 역시 개방을 통해 언질을 받았네.”
 64|
 65|“암천의 힘이 생각했던 것 이상이야. 수포로 돌아갔기에 망정이지, 만약 놈들의 계획이 성공했다면…….”
 66|
 67|무림인들, 특히 일문(一門)을 이끄는 문주와 가주들이 수십여 명씩 모이는 것은 이제 더 이상 특별한 일이 아니었다.
 68|
 69|그들은 무거운 목소리로 현재의 상황에 대해 논의하고, 앞으로의 일을 예측했다.
 70|
 71|그리고 그럴 때마다 빠지지 않고 등장하는 이름이 있었다.
 72|
 73|“열화신룡이 이번에도 대단한 활약을 펼쳤더군. 이번 일로 황실의 적극적인 원조를 얻고, 천자의 총애도 받고 있다던데.”
 74|
 75|“하면, 그 소문이 사실인가?”
 76|
 77|“어떤 소문?”
 78|
 79|“아직 듣지 못한 모양이군. 며칠 전 열화신룡이 황도를 떠날 때, 천자가 몸소 배웅까지 나와 그를 열후(列侯)에 봉했다는 소문 말일세.”
 80|
 81|“그게 무슨…… 천자가 무림인에게 벼슬을, 그것도 열후라니. 그게 가당키나 한 일인가?”
 82|
 83|“지켜본 이들이 한둘이 아닐세. 아무래도 황도이다 보니 하오문과 개방 쪽에서 정보를 입수하기까지 약간의 시간이 걸리긴 했지만, 사실인 듯하네.”
 84|
 85|발 없는 말이 천 리를 가는 법.
 86|
 87|암천을 외적으로 칭하며 전쟁을 선포한 황실의 포고문과 전례 없는 예우를 받으며 열후의 반열에 오른 진태경의 활약상은 순식간에 사람들의 입에 오르내렸다.
 88|
 89|이제는 무려 황실까지 나섰다.
 90|
 91|정마대전에도 두 손 놓고 지켜만 보고 있던 대국이, 헤아릴 수도 없을 만큼 무수한 군병과 물자를 지닌 그들이 나선다면 암천 따위는 바람 앞의 등불이나 다름없다.
 92|
 93|아니, 정확히는 모두가 그렇게 예상했다.
 94|
 95|자세한 상황을 알고 있는 소수의 몇몇 사람을 제외한다면.
 96|
 97|푸드득!
 98|
 99|거친 날갯짓과 함께 저 멀리 사라지는 전서응(傳書鷹)의 뒷모습을 지켜보던 노인은 손에 쥔 자그마한 종이를 펼쳤다.
100|
101|그의 눈동자가 깨알처럼 적힌 글자를 훑을 때마다, 얼굴에 새겨진 검상(劍傷)이 조금씩 일그러졌다.
102|
103|“그래, 그렇게 되었단 말이지.”
104|
105|마른 입술 사이로 흘러나온 나직한 뇌까림.
106|
107|한동안 제자리에서 무언가를 곰곰이 생각하던 노인은 한구석에 마련된 화로(火爐)에 들고 있던 종이를 던져넣었다.
108|
109|그리고 젖지 않도록 기름을 먹인 전서(傳書)가 순식간에 타오르는 것을 끝까지 지켜본 후, 자신이 가야 할 곳으로 걸음을 옮겼다.
110|
111|저벅. 탁.
112|
113|절뚝이는 걸음으로 나아갈 때마다 울려 퍼지는 둔탁한 소음.
114|
115|언뜻 보면 유생처럼 보이는 이들이 노인을 발견할 때마다 작게 고개를 숙였다.
116|
117|“오셨습니까, 각주(閣主).”
118|
119|“잠시, 광서에서의 일에 대해 보고드릴 것이 있습니다.”
120|
121|“남궁세가(南宮世家)에서 급보가 들어왔습니다.”
122|
123|“하북과 요녕, 그리고 섬서에서…….”
124|
125|품 안에 한가득 죽편을 들고 지나가는 이도, 짤막한 인사만 건네고 떠나는 이도 있었지만, 그들 중 대부분은 새로운 정보를 노인에게 알려 주었고 그는 그럴 때마다 머릿속의 생각을 정리하고 가다듬었다.
126|
127|그리고 마침내, 굳게 닫힌 문 앞에 섰다.
128|
129|달칵.
130|
131|마치 기다렸다는 듯이 열리는 문.
132|
133|하지만 노인은 놀라지 않았다.
134|
135|자신이 수천, 수만 리 밖의 일들을 속속들이 아는 것처럼 이 방의 주인 역시 마찬가지였으니까.
136|
137|물론 비슷하지만 실상은 차원이 달랐다.
138|
139|노인에게는 수많은 눈과 귀가 있지만, 상대는 혼자만의 힘으로 반경 백여 장 안에 벌어지는 모든 일을 파악할 수 있으니.
140|
141|“무공을 수련 중이셨습니까.”
142|
143|단출하기 그지없는 방 안으로 들어선 노인의 첫 마디에, 가부좌를 튼 채 앉아 있던 사내가 눈을 떴다.
144|
145|“그랬지. 조금 전까지는.”
146|
147|“죄송합니다. 아무래도 제가 의도치 않게 방해가 된 모양이군요.”
148|
149|“마음 쓰지 말게. 분명 그럴 만한 일이 있었을 테니.”
150|
151|싱긋 웃어 보이는 사내는 젊었다.
152|
153|기껏해야 이립(而立) 어림으로 보이는 얼굴에, 탈의한 상반신은 한껏 압축된 근육이 완벽한 균형을 자랑하고 있었다.
154|
155|물론 그마저도 옷을 걸친 순간, 어디서나 볼 수 있는 평범한 청년 중 한 사람이 되었지만.
156|
157|“그래, 무슨 일인가?”
158|
159|계속해서 흘러나오는 자연스러운 하대.
160|
161|그러나 사내에게는 그럴 만한 자격과 연륜이 충분했다.
162|
163|검성(劍星) 매종학은 천하 무림을 지탱하는 가장 거대한 기둥 중 하나니까.
164|
165|“맹주(盟主)께 급히 보고드려야 할 일이 있어 찾아뵈었습니다.”
166|
167|“급히 보고드려야 할 일이라.”
168|
169|매종학의 입가에 맺혀있던 미소가 사라졌다. 준비된 자리에 앉은 그는 찻주전자를 기울이며 말을 이었다.
170|
171|“혹 그 보고가, 산서(山西)에 관련된 일인가?”
172|
173|쪼르륵.
174|
175|차갑게 식어 있던 찻물이 잔을 채우기도 전에 김을 피워올린다. 매종학을 따라 착석한 노인은 삼매진화의 열기로 달구어진 찻잔을 어루만졌다.
176|
177|“예.”
178|
179|찻잔은 따뜻했다. 그러나 지금부터 나오는 이야기는 차갑고 어두울 것이다.
180|
181|매종학은 그 사실을 노인의 표정에서 읽었다.
182|
183|“말하게. 은영각주(隱影閣主).”
184|
185|노인, 천면호리(天面狐狸) 송호가 대답했다.
186|
187|“태원진가가 퇴각을 철회했습니다.”
188|
189|“더 자세히.”
190|
191|“산서 무림 전체가 움직이고 있습니다. 태원진가를 중심으로 삼십여 곳의 문파와 가문이 집결했고, 산서성부 역시 모든 병력을 동원하는 중입니다.”
192|
193|“음.”
194|
195|매종학은 나직이 침음성을 흘렸다.
196|
197|더는 들을 것도 없다.
198|
199|이건 말 그대로 총력전이다. 산서 무림뿐만이 아니라, 산서성 전체의 사활(死活)이 걸린 대전투가 될 것이다.
200|
201|“산서의 전력은?”
202|
203|“우선 태원진가를 필두로 오천여 명에 달하는 무인들이 대기중이고, 거기에 더하여 기병 일천을 포함한 관군 일만이 있습니다.”
204|
205|도합 만 오천.
206|
207|그야말로 바닥까지 긁어모은 병력이다.
208|
209|그마저도 지난 이 년의 시간 동안 태원진가가 놀라운 부흥을 일궈 내지 못했더라면, 무려 오천이나 되는 무인이 집결하지도 못했을 것이다.
210|
211|다만 가장 큰 문제는…….
212|
213|“적들의 절반도 되지 않는군.”
214|
215|매종학의 뇌까림에 천면호리는 무겁게 고개를 끄덕였다.
216|
217|은영각에서 파악한 바에 의하면 남하 중인 초원의 군세는 최소 삼만에서 많게는 사만으로 불어날 터.
218|
219|초원과 인접해 있는 탓에 산서성에 배치된 관군들은 상당한 정예들이지만, 전체 병력의 두 배가 넘는 기마군단의 파도는 그야말로 악몽 그 자체다.
220|
221|“피해를 최소화하기 위해 우선 북부를 비우고, 중부에서 전투를 벌일 심산인 것 같습니다.”
222|
223|“중부라면, 역시 근거지인 태원(太原)인가?”
224|
225|“정확히는 태원에서 삼백 리가량 떨어진 정양(定襄)에서 결전을 치를 듯합니다.”
226|
227|“정양이라. 정양…….”
228|
229|작게 중얼거린 매종학은 불현듯 이 왠지 모를 익숙함의 정체를 깨달았다.
230|
231|“그곳이로군. 팔천협(八天峽).”
232|
233|“예. 맞습니다.”
234|
235|천면호리가 침착한 어조로 말을 이었다.
236|
237|“팔천협은 그 자체로 천혜의 요새나 다름없지요. 과거 정마대전 당시 마교의 대군을 성공적으로 격퇴했고, 이 년 전에도 태원진가의 승리에 결정적인 공헌을 했던 장소입니다.”
238|
239|산서성의 중부와 북부의 경계선에 자리 잡은 팔천협은 항아리 모양의 협곡이다.
240|
241|길은 가파르고, 입구는 좁으니 소수로 다수의 적을 상대하기에는 최적의 전장.
242|
243|더군다나 상대의 전력 대부분이 기마병이라는 것을 감안한다면, 이만한 장소를 찾기도 힘들다.
244|
245|문제는 그 기마병의 숫자가 물경 수만에 달하는 데다가, 아직 진정한 적은 정확한 실체를 드러내지도 않았다는 것.
246|
247|“팔천협에서 결전이 벌어진다면, 태원진가가 승리할 가능성은 어느 정도라고 생각하나?”
248|
249|“높게 쳐도 이 할. 아무리 전황이 태원진가 측에 유리하게 흘러간다 해도 그 이상은 힘듭니다.”
250|

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

## Glossary

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

## Output contract

Return exactly one JSON object and no Markdown fence or prose:

{
"chapter": 1,
"decisions": [
{
"hunk_id": "H001",
"decision": "SOL",
"reason": "brief specific reason"
},
{
"hunk_id": "H002",
"decision": "BASE",
"reason": "brief specific reason"
},
{
"hunk_id": "H003",
"decision": "REPAIR",
"replacement": "complete replacement English for this hunk",
"reason": "brief specific reason"
}
]
}

Include exactly one decision for every numbered hunk, in hunk order. `replacement` is required only for `REPAIR`.

Reasons must name the veto, or say that SOL keeps sense and voice. Do not merely say one version is "better" or "more natural" without stating what changed.

Keep reasons brief. Do not adjudicate unchanged passages. Do not call tools.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

A catastrophe beyond anything the hundred thousand Demonic Cultists who had trampled the Central Plains decades ago could have brought was looming over them.

[P29]
And those within the world of the Murim felt the reality of it more keenly than anyone.

[P30]
“I hear they’ve reached all the way into the Imperial Court. They’ve been at it for decades, since around the Great Faction War.”

[P31]
“I heard the same from the Beggars’ Sect.”

[P32]
“Dark Heaven is stronger than we thought. It’s a good thing their plan fell through. If it had succeeded…”

[P33]
It was no longer unusual for dozens of martial artists to gather, especially Sect Leaders and Family Heads.

[P34]
They discussed the situation in grave voices and tried to predict what would come next.

[P35]
And one name came up every time.

[P36]
“The Blazing Flame Divine Dragon distinguished himself again. I hear this earned him the Imperial Court’s active support and the Son of Heaven’s favor.”

[P37]
“Then is that rumor true?”

[P38]
“What rumor?”

[P39]
“You haven’t heard? A few days ago, when the Blazing Flame Divine Dragon left the Imperial Capital, the Son of Heaven himself came out to see him off and made him a marquis.”

[P40]
“What? The Son of Heaven gave a martial artist an official title—and made him a marquis, no less? Is that even possible?”

[P41]
“There were plenty of witnesses. It happened in the Imperial Capital, so it took the Lower District Sect and the Beggars’ Sect a little time to get word of it, but it seems to be true.”

[P42]
News travels a thousand li without feet.

[P43]
The Imperial Court’s proclamation declaring Dark Heaven a foreign enemy and announcing war, together with word of Jin Taekyung’s achievements and the unprecedented honor of his elevation to marquis, spread from mouth to mouth in no time.

[P44]
Now even the Imperial Court had stepped in.

[P45]
The Great Nation had stood by even during the Great Faction War. If a power with more soldiers and supplies than anyone could count joined the fight, Dark Heaven would be no more than a candle in the wind.

[P46]
Or rather, that was what everyone expected.

[P47]
Everyone except the handful of people who knew the full situation.

[P48]
Flap, flap!

[P49]
The old man watched a messenger eagle disappear into the distance, its wings beating hard, then unfolded the tiny scrap of paper in his hand.

[P50]
As his eyes moved over the minuscule writing, the sword scar on his face twisted little by little.

[P51]
“So that’s how it is.”

[P52]
The quiet words slipped between his dry lips.

[P53]
He stood there for a while, deep in thought, then tossed the paper into a brazier in one corner.

[P54]
He watched until the oil-treated missive, prepared to keep it dry, had burned away. Then he set off for his destination.

[P55]
Thud. Tap.

[P56]
A dull sound echoed with each limping step.

[P57]
Men who looked like Confucian scholars bowed their heads slightly whenever they saw him.

[P58]
“Welcome, Chief of the Hidden Shadow Pavilion.”

[P59]
“I have a brief report on what happened in Guangxi.”

[P60]
“We’ve received an urgent message from the Nangong Family.”

[P61]
“And from Hebei, Liaoning, and Shaanxi…”

[P62]
Some passed with their arms full of bamboo slips; others offered only a brief greeting before moving on. Most, however, brought the old man new information. With each report, he sorted and refined his thoughts.

[P63]
At last, he stopped before a firmly shut door.

[P64]
Click.

[P65]
The door opened as though someone had been waiting for him.

[P66]
But the old man wasn’t surprised.

[P67]
Just as he knew the details of events thousands, even tens of thousands, of li away, the master of this room knew what happened around him.

[P68]
There was a resemblance, though the scale of their abilities was entirely different.

[P69]
The old man had countless eyes and ears. The man inside could sense everything happening within a radius of over a hundred jang by his own power alone.

[P70]
“Were you practicing martial arts?”

[P71]
At the old man’s first words as he entered the exceedingly plain room, the man sitting cross-legged opened his eyes.

[P72]
“I was. Until just now.”

[P73]
“I’m sorry. It seems I interrupted you without meaning to.”

[P74]
“Don’t worry about it. I’m sure you had good reason.”

[P75]
The man smiled. He was young.

[P76]
He looked barely thirty, and the compact muscles of his bare upper body were perfectly balanced.

[P77]
Of course, once he put on his clothes, he looked like any ordinary young man.

[P78]
“So, what is it?”

[P79]
He continued to speak to the old man with the easy familiarity of a senior.

[P80]
But he had more than enough standing and years behind him to do so.

[P81]
Sword Saint Mae Jonghak was one of the greatest pillars supporting the Murim.

[P82]
“I’ve come because there’s something I must report to the Alliance Leader at once.”

[P83]
“Something urgent.”

[P84]
The smile faded from Mae Jonghak’s lips. He took his seat and tilted a teapot as he went on.

[P85]
“Is it about Shanxi?”

[P86]
Trickle.

[P87]
Steam rose from the cold tea before it had even filled the cup. The old man sat down across from Mae Jonghak and touched the teacup, warmed by Samadhi True Fire.

[P88]
“Yes.”

[P89]
The cup was warm. The news to come would be cold and dark.

[P90]
Mae Jonghak could see it in the old man’s face.

[P91]
“Tell me, Chief of the Hidden Shadow Pavilion.”

[P92]
The old man—Song Ho, the Thousand-Faced Fox—answered.

[P93]
“The Jin Family of Taiyuan has called off its retreat.”

[P94]
“Go on.”

[P95]
“All of Shanxi Murim is mobilizing. Some thirty sects and families have gathered around the Jin Family of Taiyuan, and the Shanxi Provincial Office is mobilizing every available troop.”

[P96]
“Hmm.”

[P97]
Mae Jonghak let out a low hum.

[P98]
He hardly needed to hear more.

[P99]
This was an all-out war. Not just Shanxi Murim, but all of Shanxi Province would live or die by the coming battle.

[P100]
“What forces does Shanxi have?”

[P101]
“About five thousand martial artists are standing by, led by the Jin Family of Taiyuan. The government has another ten thousand troops, including a thousand cavalry.”

[P102]
Fifteen thousand in all.

[P103]
They had scraped together every last man.

[P104]
Even that would not have included five thousand martial artists if the Jin Family of Taiyuan had not made such an extraordinary resurgence over the past two years.

[P105]
But the greatest problem was…

[P106]
“Not even half the enemy’s numbers.”

[P107]
At Mae Jonghak’s mutter, the Thousand-Faced Fox nodded grimly.

[P108]
According to the Hidden Shadow Pavilion’s intelligence, the grassland army marching south would swell to at least thirty thousand, perhaps as many as forty thousand.

[P109]
Shanxi Province bordered the grasslands, so the government troops stationed there were seasoned soldiers. But a wave of cavalry more than twice the size of their entire force was a nightmare in itself.

[P110]
“They seem to intend to evacuate the north first and fight in the central region to minimize casualties.”

[P111]
“The central region. Taiyuan, their stronghold?”

[P112]
“More precisely, they appear to be planning a decisive battle at Jeongyang, about three hundred li from Taiyuan.”

[P113]
“Jeongyang. Jeongyang…”

[P114]
Mae Jonghak murmured the name, then suddenly realized why it sounded familiar.

[P115]
“That’s where Eight Spring Gorge is.”

[P116]
“Yes.”

[P117]
The Thousand-Faced Fox continued calmly.

[P118]
“Eight Spring Gorge is a natural fortress. During the Great Faction War, the Demonic Cult’s great army was successfully repelled there. Two years ago, it also played a decisive part in the Jin Family of Taiyuan’s victory.”

[P119]
Eight Spring Gorge lay on the boundary between central and northern Shanxi Province. It was shaped like a jar.

[P120]
The path was steep and the entrance narrow, making it an ideal battlefield for a small force facing a larger one.

[P121]
Considering that most of the enemy were cavalry, they could hardly find a better place.

[P122]
The problem was that those cavalry numbered in the tens of thousands—and the true enemy had yet to show its face.

[P123]
“If the decisive battle is fought at Eight Spring Gorge, what chance do you give the Jin Family of Taiyuan?”

[P124]
“Twenty percent at best. Even if the battle goes in their favor, I can’t put it any higher.”

[P125]
The Thousand-Faced Fox’s answer was firm, his gaze darkening.

[P126]
“If the enemy army consisted only of nomads, I’d put their chances above fifty percent. But…”

[P127]
“Right. We can’t forget them.”

[P128]
Dark Heaven.

[P129]
Pitch-black clouds had swallowed even the blue skies over the grasslands. Their presence alone held everyone fast, like a trap around their ankles.

[P130]
“As things stand, we can’t expect to send the Jin Family of Taiyuan any support.”

[P131]
The Thousand-Faced Fox’s face was dark as he said it.

[P132]
As the Murim Alliance Leader’s right hand and head of the Hidden Shadow Pavilion, he understood the state of the world better than most.

[P133]
“Everyone knows what could happen if we move rashly. We could be caught in their dark arts and suffer a terrible blow.”

[P134]
It defied common sense, but Dark Heaven had already used the dark art known as the Moving Formation several times.

[P135]
Shaolin, the Mount Tai and Northern Dipper of the Murim, had suffered devastating losses because of it. The Nine Sects and One Gang and the Five Great Families were no less vulnerable.

[P136]
Not even here in Henan, where the Murim Alliance headquarters stood, was safe.

[P137]
“Then the forces we can mobilize right now…”

[P138]
“None.”

[P139]
“None?”

[P140]
Mae Jonghak gazed steadily at the Thousand-Faced Fox, who had answered without a moment’s hesitation.

[P141]
“I want to ask you one thing. Think carefully before you answer.”

[P142]
“Ask.”

[P143]
“When you say we have no troops to send to Shanxi, is that the absolute truth?”

[P144]
“…!”

[P145]
The Thousand-Faced Fox chose silence.

[P146]
He had lived a life worthy of his epithet.

[P147]
Hiding his identity and telling brazen lies as though they were the truth came as naturally to him as breathing.

[P148]
But even he could not bring himself to lie under the clear gaze of Sword Saint Mae Jonghak.

[P149]
“You already know, Alliance Leader…”

[P150]
The Thousand-Faced Fox spoke at last, his voice heavy.

[P151]
“The balance of power has tipped too far. Helping Shanxi now would be a poor decision. You should formally order the Jin Family of Taiyuan to retreat at once.”

[P152]
“I think it’s too late.”

[P153]
“It isn’t. Time is short, but if we pull the front line back to Henan without delay, we can preserve our remaining forces and plan for what comes next.”

[P154]
“No. It’s too late.”

[P155]
Mae Jonghak shook his head slightly.

[P156]
“Too late to change their minds.”

[P157]
“…!”

[P158]
“The Lesser Family Head of the Jin Family of Taiyuan is an astute man. He takes a broad view of every situation and is exceedingly careful before making a decision. Isn’t that why you recommended him to the Murim Alliance’s strategy division?”

[P159]
The Thousand-Faced Fox let out a low groan before he could stop himself.

[P160]
If a man that cautious had staked his family’s fate on a decision, he would never take it back.

[P161]
Not even on the Murim Alliance Leader’s orders.

[P162]
“But if this continues, we could lose Shanxi. We could lose them all.”

[P163]
“I know. And I know that if they retreat now, the innocent people who haven’t managed to flee will be massacred.”

[P164]
“…!”

[P165]
“Don’t look away from it. They aren’t fighting only to protect the place they call home.”

[P166]
At a loss for words, the Thousand-Faced Fox closed his eyes, unable to meet Mae Jonghak’s gaze.

[P167]
Yes.

[P168]
He knew. He had only pretended not to.

[P169]
This was not a battle. It was a war.

[P170]
To win this war, a few thousand martial artists mattered more than over a hundred thousand commoners.

[P171]
“Was my judgment…wrong?”

[P172]
“No. It was excellent. You’re a better strategist than anyone I know.”

[P173]
At the unexpected answer, the Thousand-Faced Fox opened his eyes.

[P174]
Mae Jonghak was looking at him with a gentle smile.

[P175]
“You simply forgot one thing.”

[P176]
“What was it?”

[P177]
“You were so busy looking at the whole forest that you missed a small branch within it.”

[P178]
At that very moment—

[P179]
Srrk.

[P180]
With a motion of Mae Jonghak’s hand, qi reached out and flung open the firmly shut door.

[P181]
A faint, stealthy presence followed, and a figure swept into the room like the wind.

[P182]
“Well? What news have you brought?”

[P183]
Mae Jonghak sounded as though he had been waiting for him. The messenger from the Alliance Leader’s Office prostrated himself and answered.

[P184]
“Urgent news! The Hebei Peng Family, the Murong Family, Huashan, and the Zhongnan Sect are each sending two thousand reinforcements to save Shanxi Province—”

[P185]
The Thousand-Faced Fox froze. He heard nothing more.

[P186]
They were sending that many reinforcements when their own strongholds might be in danger?

[P187]
It went against every principle of warfare he had learned. Against plain common sense.

[P188]
But…

[P189]
*So that’s what it was.*

[P190]
The Thousand-Faced Fox smiled bitterly.

[P191]
Only after the messenger had left did he break the long silence.

[P192]
“I understand now. I know the name of the branch I failed to see.”

[P193]
“What is it?”

[P194]
“Chivalry.”

[P195]
Mae Jonghak smiled gently.

[P196]
He remembered his younger self, who had sworn to cultivate martial skill in the service of chivalry.

[P197]
“Never forget again. We’re all martial artists.”

[P198]
That day, with the Double Ninth Festival four days away, two thousand martial artists left the Murim Alliance headquarters and headed north.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

## Glossary

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

[P142]
“Ask.”

[P143]
“When you say we have no troops to send to Shanxi, is that the absolute truth?”

[P144]
“…!”

[P145]
The Thousand-Faced Fox chose silence.

[P146]
He had lived a life worthy of his epithet.

[P147]
Hiding his identity and telling brazen lies as though they were the truth came as naturally to him as breathing.

[P148]
But even he could not bring himself to lie under the clear gaze of Sword Saint Mae Jonghak.

[P149]
“You already know, Alliance Leader…”

[P150]
The Thousand-Faced Fox spoke at last, his voice heavy.

[P151]
“The balance of power has tipped too far. Helping Shanxi now would be a poor decision. You should formally order the Jin Family of Taiyuan to retreat at once.”

[P152]
“I think it’s too late.”

[P153]
“It isn’t. Time is short, but if we pull the front line back to Henan without delay, we can preserve our remaining forces and plan for what comes next.”

[P154]
“No. It’s too late.”

[P155]
Mae Jonghak shook his head slightly.

[P156]
“Too late to change their minds.”

[P157]
“…!”

[P158]
“The Lesser Family Head of the Jin Family of Taiyuan is an astute man. He takes a broad view of every situation and is exceedingly careful before making a decision. Isn’t that why you recommended him to the Murim Alliance’s strategy division?”

[P159]
The Thousand-Faced Fox let out a low groan before he could stop himself.

[P160]
If a man that cautious had staked his family’s fate on a decision, he would never take it back.

[P161]
Not even on the Murim Alliance Leader’s orders.

[P162]
“But if this continues, we could lose Shanxi. We could lose them all.”

[P163]
“I know. And I know that if they retreat now, the innocent people who haven’t managed to flee will be massacred.”

[P164]
“…!”

[P165]
“Don’t look away from it. They aren’t fighting only to protect the place they call home.”

[P166]
At a loss for words, the Thousand-Faced Fox closed his eyes, unable to meet Mae Jonghak’s gaze.

[P167]
Yes.

[P168]
He knew. He had only pretended not to.

[P169]
This was not a battle. It was a war.

[P170]
To win this war, a few thousand martial artists mattered more than over a hundred thousand commoners.

[P171]
“Was my judgment…wrong?”

[P172]
“No. It was excellent. You’re a better strategist than anyone I know.”

[P173]
At the unexpected answer, the Thousand-Faced Fox opened his eyes.

[P174]
Mae Jonghak was looking at him with a gentle smile.

[P175]
“You simply forgot one thing.”

[P176]
“What was it?”

[P177]
“You were so busy looking at the whole forest that you missed a small branch within it.”

[P178]
At that very moment—

[P179]
Srrk.

[P180]
With a motion of Mae Jonghak’s hand, qi reached out and flung open the firmly shut door.

[P181]
A faint, stealthy presence followed, and a figure swept into the room like the wind.

[P182]
“Well? What news have you brought?”

[P183]
Mae Jonghak sounded as though he had been waiting for him. The messenger from the Alliance Leader’s Office prostrated himself and answered.

[P184]
“Urgent news! The Hebei Peng Family, the Murong Family, Huashan, and the Zhongnan Sect are each sending two thousand reinforcements to save Shanxi Province—”

[P185]
The Thousand-Faced Fox froze. He heard nothing more.

[P186]
They were sending that many reinforcements when their own strongholds might be in danger?

[P187]
It went against every principle of warfare he had learned. Against plain common sense.

[P188]
But…

[P189]
*So that’s what it was.*

[P190]
The Thousand-Faced Fox smiled bitterly.

[P191]
Only after the messenger had left did he break the long silence.

[P192]
“I understand now. I know the name of the branch I failed to see.”

[P193]
“What is it?”

[P194]
“Chivalry.”

[P195]
Mae Jonghak smiled gently.

[P196]
He remembered his younger self, who had sworn to cultivate martial skill in the service of chivalry.

[P197]
“Never forget again. We’re all martial artists.”

[P198]
That day, with the Double Ninth Festival four days away, two thousand martial artists left the Murim Alliance headquarters and headed north.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.

- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
